Project API Reference

Flask Backend (app.py)

ctrlX CORE Data Layer Console Client.

This module provides a command-line interface to interact with the Bosch Rexroth ctrlX CORE Data Layer REST API. It allows querying system metrics and changing the controller’s operating state.

app.change_scheduler_state(target_state: str) → bool[source]

Change the scheduler operating state (OPERATING, SETUP, SERVICE).

Sends a PUT request to the ‘scheduler/admin/state’ node using the exact payload structure analyzed from the ctrlX Web-UI network request.

Parameters:

target_state (str) – The target state (‘OPERATING’, ‘SETUP’, ‘SERVICE’).

Returns:

True if state transition was successful and verified, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

app.configure_connection() → None[source]

Prompt the user for ctrlX CORE connection details.

If the user presses Enter without typing, fallback standard values (IP: ‘192.168.1.1’, User/Password: ‘boschrexroth’) are applied. The password input is masked for security.

app.fetch_bearer_token() → bool[source]

Authenticate against the Identity Manager of the ctrlX CORE.

Retrieves a valid Bearer token and updates the global HTTP session headers for all subsequent API calls.

Returns:

True if authentication succeeded, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

app.main() → None[source]

Execute the main application loop.

Handles the CLI menu routing and manages the connection states.

app.read_datalayer_value(path: str) → dict | None[source]

Read a value from a specific ctrlX Data Layer node.

Parameters:

path (str) – The Data Layer node path (e.g., ‘scheduler/admin/state’).

Returns:

The JSON response dictionary from the node if successful, None otherwise.

Return type:

dict or None

app.show_menu() → str[source]

Display the interactive main console menu.

Returns:

The user’s menu choice as a string.

Return type:

str

Deployment Automation (install_snap.py)

ctrlX CORE App (Snap) Deployment Automation Script.

This module provides a robust command-line interface to automate the installation and management of Snap applications on Bosch Rexroth ctrlX CORE devices via the Package Manager REST API.

install_snap.change_scheduler_state(target_state: str) → bool[source]

Request a change of the scheduler operating state.

Iterates through multiple known API payload formats to ensure compatibility across various ctrlX OS firmware versions. Caches the successful format for subsequent calls.

Parameters:

target_state (str) – The requested scheduler state (‘OPERATING’, ‘SETUP’, ‘SERVICE’).

Returns:

True if the API accepted the state transition command, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

install_snap.check_active_tasks() → bool[source]

Query the Package Manager API for any currently active background tasks.

Checks if any installation, update, or maintenance task is running or pending, which might block Scheduler state transitions or other concurrent actions.

Returns:

True if an active or pending task exists, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

install_snap.check_architecture_compatibility(snap_path: str, expected_arch: str) → bool[source]

Verify if the Snap filename is compatible with the controller’s architecture.

Extracts architectural markers from the file name and compares them with the target architecture to prevent operational risks or system faults.

Parameters:

  • snap_path (str) – The local file path to the .snap package.

  • expected_arch (str) – The target CPU architecture resolved from the controller (‘arm’ or ‘amd64’).

Returns:

True if the architecture matches or the user explicitly overrides the mismatch, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

install_snap.configure_connection() → None[source]

Prompt the user for ctrlX CORE connection details.

Applies default connection parameters (IP: ‘192.168.1.1’, User/Password: ‘boschrexroth’) upon pressing Enter. Masking is applied to the password input for security.

install_snap.fetch_bearer_token() → bool[source]

Authenticate against the Identity Manager of the ctrlX CORE.

Retrieves a valid OAuth2 Bearer token and updates the global HTTP session headers for all subsequent API requests.

Returns:

True if authentication succeeded, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

install_snap.get_controller_info() → tuple[str, str][source]

Read the electronic typeplate to determine the hardware model and architecture.

Queries the system typeplate API and parses the response to identify whether the target hardware is an ARM-based or AMD64-based controller.

Returns:

A tuple containing the resolved model name and the expected architecture.

Return type:

tuple[str, str]

install_snap.get_installed_app_info(app_name: str) → dict | None[source]

Check if the specified application is already installed on the controller.

Queries the package manager API to retrieve all currently installed packages, filtering the list by the given application name (with typical ‘snap_’ prefix normalization).

Parameters:

app_name (str) – The name of the application to check.

Returns:

The package metadata dictionary if installed, None otherwise.

Return type:

dict or None

install_snap.get_scheduler_state() → str | None[source]

Retrieve the current Scheduler operating state from the Data Layer.

Queries the Data Layer node ‘scheduler/admin/state’ and extracts the active state value.

Returns:

The active scheduler state string (e.g., ‘OPERATING’, ‘SETUP’, ‘SERVICE’) or None if the query fails.

Return type:

str or None

install_snap.get_task_status(task_id: str) → dict | None[source]

Retrieve the status of a background package manager task.

Parameters:

task_id (str) – The unique identifier of the task.

Returns:

The raw task metadata dictionary if found, None otherwise.

Return type:

dict or None

install_snap.install_snap(snap_path: str) → bool[source]

Upload the Snap file to the Package Manager API and monitor the installation task.

Performs a multipart/form-data upload of the local Snap binary. If accepted (HTTP 202), it extracts the task ID from either the JSON response body or the Location header, and initiates the task polling loop.

Parameters:

snap_path (str) – The local path to the .snap file.

Returns:

True if the package was successfully uploaded and installed, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

install_snap.main() → None[source]

Execute the automated app installation workflow.

Runs pre-flight validation checks, manages Scheduler state transitions safely (including retries during lockouts), uploads and polls the installation task, and restores the controller’s state back to OPERATING mode.

install_snap.wait_for_scheduler_state(target_state: str, timeout_seconds: int = 60) → bool[source]

Poll the Scheduler operating state until it reaches the target state.

Parameters:

  • target_state (str) – The expected target state.

  • timeout_seconds (int) – The maximum duration in seconds to wait before timing out, defaults to 60.

Returns:

True if the target state was successfully reached within the timeout, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool

install_snap.wait_for_task_completion(task_id: str, timeout_seconds: int = 300) → bool[source]

Poll the task status endpoint until the installation task is complete.

Monitors progress percentage and status strings. Implements protections for hangups at 100% and automated cleanup behaviors of completed tasks.

Parameters:

  • task_id (str) – The unique identifier of the task to poll.

  • timeout_seconds (int) – The maximum duration in seconds to wait, defaults to 300.

Returns:

True if the installation task finished successfully, False otherwise.

Return type:

bool
